_comment:
Source definitions. JSON, not YAML — ruled 2026-08-07 (Q22). Keyed by source name, so a duplicate name is unwritable rather than merely discouraged. Underscore-prefixed keys are comments; every other unknown key is a hard validation error. Use the /add-source skill to onboard a new one.

HARD RULE 1 — EVERY source below is `enabled: false` and every url is the REMPLACER placeholder, because no endpoint in this file has been verified against the live site. CLAUDE.md hard rule 1 forbids writing an endpoint from memory, and the loader REFUSES an enabled source whose url still contains REMPLACER — so this file cannot be half-enabled by accident. Unblocking a source needs a DevTools cURL capture from the developer; docs/SOURCES.md records which sites answer a plain client and which 403 it.
_why: The single flag that disarms the fail-closed rule of CLAUDE.md §1. It is REQUIRED on every block — the loader refuses a source that omits it, and SourceProfile independently defaults it to true. `false` is a claim that this landlord publishes NO social stock whatsoever, and it is only defensible for In'li (Action Logement's intermediate arm) and the private-market portals. Every value here is bound to tests/fixtures/tenure/corpus.json by ConfigTest, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

inli._comment: A1, docs/SOURCES.md. The flagship: ~60 000 LLI units across IDF, covers both 78 and 95, rents 20-30% below market. Pure LLI, which is why mixed_tenure is false here and almost nowhere else. THE FIRST VERIFIED SOURCE IN THIS FILE (2026-08-19).
inli._source: Fetched from the live site, robots.txt read FIRST: `User-agent: *` / `Disallow: /espace-membre/` only, so /locations/ is allowed and this poll is within hard rule 5. The search page is SERVER-RENDERED — there is no JSON API behind it (the route map at /locations/js/routes and the app bundle expose only member-area endpoints), which is why type is `html` and not `json`. Frozen payload: tests/fixtures/inli/search.html, scrubbed of the page's embedded third-party Google API key.
inli._why: WHY THE FILTERS ARE LOOSER THAN criteria.json (ruled 2026-08-19): In'li applies price_max/area_min/room_min server-side, so anything it rejects never reaches CriteriaEngine — no score, no log, no `à vérifier` entry. That is the silent over-rejection hard rule 8 warns about, and it is invisible precisely because nothing arrives. So the URL casts a WIDE net and criteria.json does the real filtering, where every rejection is scored and logged; tightening your criteria later then needs no re-capture. WHY PAGINATION: measured, not assumed — these filters returned `92 logements` across 4 pages of 24 [2026-08-19]. A page-one-only read would have dropped 68 listings on every pass and reported a healthy run. total_selector is what makes the walk checkable: collecting fewer than the page declares is a hard failure, because a page=N that quietly 404s ends the walk exactly like a real last page.

map._comment: Selectors, not dotted paths — see src/php/Adapters/Html/Selector.php. `=>` introduces a capture, because the card packs rooms and surface into ONE text node (`3 pièces · 55.32 m²`) and a general number parser would return whichever comes first.
map._charges_included: The card prints `cc` in a sibling span beside the figure — charges comprises, confirmed on all 19 cards of the frozen capture.

icf_novedis._comment: A2. ICF Habitat's non-social arm — 10 000 units aimed at households above the social ceilings. SNCF group, so stock clusters on rail corridors, which fits the boucle de Seine. mixed_tenure stays TRUE (Q20, ruled 2026-08-07): `false` would be right for a Novedis-only endpoint and wrong for the group portal, and nothing here yet says which the adapter will hit. Costs a few digest entries; cannot cost an application.

cdc_habitat._comment: A3. robots.txt disallows /Recherche/show/, which is very likely the search-results path (Q15, ruled 2026-08-07). Stays disabled until the real endpoint path is known to sit OUTSIDE that Disallow. If it does not, CDC Habitat moves to the email-alert route like a private portal. Never work around a robots.txt (hard rule 5).

seqens._comment: A5. Action Logement group, strong 78/95 footprint. robots.txt clean (/wp-admin/ only). Publishes social AND intermediate stock on the same pages — see CLAUDE.md, 'The Action Logement wrinkle'.

seloger._comment: B1. Largest IDF inventory. Private market, so LIBRE — in scope since the Q4 answer. type is email_alert because direct scraping of a private portal is opt-in, disabled by default and refuses to run without an explicit flag (hard rule 4); the email-alert route is within ToS, defeats anti-bot because there is no bot, and fires on publication rather than on a poll.

leboncoin._comment: B2. Where non-agency private landlords actually post. 403s a plain client, so email alert is the only route regardless of preference.

fixture_demo._comment: NOT a real landlord. A frozen-payload source that exercises the whole pipeline end to end offline — config load, fetch, field map, classify, criteria, dedup, store, notify — with no network and no credentials. It is what makes `scout run --once` verifiable before any real endpoint is captured, and it is enabled BECAUSE it reads a committed file rather than the internet. mixed_tenure is true so the fixture exercises the fail-closed path, which is the half that matters.

email_demo._comment: NOT a real portal. A frozen ALERT-EMAIL source, the mailbox twin of fixture_demo: it exercises the whole email-alert path — IMAP-shaped mailbox, MIME parse, charset conversion, link extraction, classify, criteria, notify — with no credentials and no network. Enabled because it reads committed .eml files. Point MAILBOX_DIR at tests/fixtures/mailbox to run it; set IMAP_HOST instead and the same source reads a real mailbox with no other change.
